workLog.activity: Traced why comparison.head and endingCommit drift
workLog.finding: The committed schema already documents the divergence the check rejects. session-log.schema.json:170-174 defines commitHead as the "Latest commit authored by this session when QA rebinding advances comparison.head", and extract_session_episode.py:831-832 carries the same reading. endingCommit moves on an unrelated schedule under session-logs.md MUST 2 and MUST 3.

workLog.activity: Measured the blast radius of the binding commit after ADR-096
workLog.finding: QaBinding.commit is barely load-bearing now. validate_qa_report() reads expected.session_log and never expected.commit, and validate_session_json.py uses binding.commit only when live-HEAD resolution fails, since validation_head auto-resolves earlier in the same function. The raise was blocking the whole QA-evidence check to protect a value that is normally never read, which is what argues against a mechanical ADR-096 copy.

workLog.activity: Delegated ADR authoring, implementation, and a self-reviewed single-pass debate to an orchestrator subagent
workLog.finding: The orchestrator produced ADR-099, the code change, tests, and a mirror regeneration, then disclosed honestly that its own adr-review pass was a single session applying six lenses sequentially, not six independent agents, because the harness serving that subagent registered no subagent-spawn tool. It recommended re-running the real debate on a harness with the tooling rather than fabricating a 6/6 tally.

workLog.activity: Ran the genuine six-agent adr-review debate from the orchestrating session, which does have Agent-tool access
workLog.finding: Six independent Phase-1 reviewers (architect, critic, independent-thinker, security, analyst, high-level-advisor) read the ADR and the live repository blind to each other. Five returned Accept or Disagree-and-Commit; independent-thinker returned Block, arguing the Context section's central claim (the two fields move independently) was contradicted by a measured 38-of-38 lockstep pattern. A Phase 2 conflict-resolution pass (high-level-advisor, tie-breaker) tested and rejected a selection-bias explanation for that measurement, corrected the figure to 42 of 44, confirmed the Context claim did not hold, and overruled the Block against the Decision (which does not depend on it) while upholding it against the Context, which was rewritten.

workLog.activity: Ran a scoped Phase 4 convergence check (independent-thinker, analyst) against the rewrite
workLog.finding: analyst returned Accept after independently re-deriving the corpus table and catching two trivial stale figures. independent-thinker returned Disagree-and-Commit, having found the rewrite's own replacement claim overstated the lockstep pattern again: 34 of the 42 agreeing edits are a session log's first commit (fields born equal, nothing moved), not hand-syncs; only 8 are edits to an already-committed log, 7 of which are the genuine pattern. This session independently reproduced 42/44 and the 34/8 split against git log --all -- .agents/sessions/ before applying the correction, confirming both figures exactly.

workLog.activity: Merged origin/main into the branch to pick up PR #5219 and resolved the resulting conflict
workLog.finding: origin/main had landed an independent fix for the same defect this branch already fixed: tests/ci/test_validate_vendor_provenance.py's stale hardcoded setup-uv SHA. Combined both approaches (parse the workflow YAML per testing.md MUST 9, assert a SHA-pattern rather than one exact SHA per the staleness lesson from PR #5215) rather than picking one side. The merge also pulled in an unrelated pip-audit CVE fix this branch had already carried (PYSEC-2026-3721) with no conflict. Per ADR-096's documented merge-diff behavior, post_qa_code_changes then correctly reported the QA report as stale, since git log -m diffs a merge commit against both parents and the branch's own prior changes reappear as new relative to a pre-merge qaCommit. Rebound qaCommit to the merge commit (c6d7f388f) after re-running uv run pytest tests/test_validate_session_json.py -q clean at 379 passed, and confirmed uv run --frozen python -c "...validate_session_end..." returns PASS/True against the rebound report.

workLog.activity: Push rejected a second time by merge-tree-ratchet after origin/main advanced again mid-push
workLog.finding: The first push attempt's pre-push suite passed every job including python-tests (632.70s) but failed pre-pr-validation; a retry moments later failed faster on merge-tree-ratchet instead, both truncated to their last captured lines so the actual cause was not visible from the push output alone. Running merge_tree_ratchet_check.py --base-ref origin/main directly showed the real cause: origin/main had landed PR #5225 (ce4860ea6), which applied the identical pip 26.1.2-to-26.2 bump this branch already carried, under different comment wording, so git merge-tree reported a conflict. Merged origin/main, resolved the one-line comment conflict in .github/workflows/pytest.yml by keeping origin/main's wording (cites issue #5222, matches what is already on main), re-ran uv run pytest tests/test_validate_session_json.py -q clean at 379 passed, confirmed merge_tree_ratchet_check.py now reports OK, and rebound the QA report's qaCommit to the new merge commit (06fa514b5).

workLog.activity: Diagnosed a stale-PR-body false failure on Validate PR, caused by rerun_failed_jobs replaying a stale event snapshot
workLog.finding: After the .github/workflows/pytest.yml merge conflict absorbed PR #5225's version, that file no longer differed from origin/main, so the PR description's ## Changes bullet mentioning it became a CRITICAL description-vs-diff mismatch. Fixed by rewriting the PR body. The first re-check used rerun_failed_jobs on the original failed run, which replayed the ORIGINAL pull_request event's snapshotted PR_BODY (still the pre-fix text), failing identically. The PR edit itself had fired a fresh pull_request.edited run with the corrected body, but a concurrency group cancelled it in favor of the stale rerun. Fix: rerun_workflow_run on the cancelled fresh run instead of rerunning the stale one.
